Find the gradient of the normal to the curve $y = 4^x$ at the point where $x = 1$.
questions.answer:
$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = (\ln 4)\,4^x$. At $x = 1$, the gradient of the tangent is $4\ln 4$, so the gradient of the normal is
$$-\frac{1}{4\ln 4} = -\frac{1}{\ln 256}.$$

questions.answer:
For the logs to exist, $x > 2$. Then $\log_3(x - 2)^2 = 2\log_3(x - 2)$:
$$2\log_3(x - 2) = 1 + \log_3(x - 2) \implies \log_3(x - 2) = 1 \implies x - 2 = 3 \implies x = 5.$$

The diagram shows the cross-section of a valley. $A$ and $C$ are the points at the top of each side of the valley, and $B$ is the lowest point in the valley. $D$ is the point vertically above $B$ and horizontally level with $A$.

From $B$ the angle of elevation of $C$ is $36^\circ$ and from $C$ the angle of depression of $D$ is $15^\circ$. The distance $AB = 314$ m and $AD = 240$ m.

The diagram shows the cross-section of a valley. $A$ and $C$ are the points at the top of each side of the valley, and $B$ is the lowest point in the valley. $D$ is the point vertically above $B$ and horizontally level with $A$.

From $B$ the angle of elevation of $C$ is $36^\circ$ and from $C$ the angle of depression of $D$ is $15^\circ$. The distance $AB = 314$ m and $AD = 240$ m.

$BD \approx 202.47$ m. Calculate the distance $CD$ correct to the nearest metre.
questions.answer:
In $\triangle CBD$: $\angle DBC = 90^\circ - 36^\circ = 54^\circ$ and $\angle BCD = 36^\circ - 15^\circ = 21^\circ$ (angle of elevation of $C$ from $B$ minus angle of depression of $D$ from $C$). Sine rule:
$$\frac{CD}{\sin 54^\circ} = \frac{BD}{\sin 21^\circ} \implies CD = \frac{202.47\sin 54^\circ}{\sin 21^\circ} \approx 457\ \text{m}.$$

A charity holds its regular fundraising drive, and records the donations received each week for the first four weeks after the drive is launched: \$2700 in week 1, \$1800 in week 2, \$1200 in week 3 and \$800 in week 4.

The director of the charity notices that the amount of donations received each week follows a geometric series. She makes some predictions on the future donations, by assuming that the same pattern will be followed.

The common ratio is $\frac23$. She claims that the drive will never raise more than \$8100 in total. Explain how she can make this prediction and why she decides to launch a new drive after thirteen weeks.
questions.answer:
Since $|r| < 1$ the series has a limiting sum:
$$S_\infty = \frac{2700}{1 - \frac23} = \$8100,$$
so the total can never exceed \$8100.

$S_{13} = \dfrac{2700\left(1 - \left(\frac23\right)^{13}\right)}{\frac13} \approx \$8058$, only about \$42 short of the maximum, and the week-13 donation is only $T_{13} = 2700\left(\frac23\right)^{12} \approx \$21$. Almost nothing more will be raised, so it makes sense to relaunch.

A two-metre-wide arched door in a restaurant is in the shape of a rectangle with a segment of a circle above it. The top of the door is the arc of a circle with radius 2 metres and its centre is in the middle of the base of the door. As shown in the diagram, the radii to the top corners of the door each make an angle of $\frac\pi3$ with the base, and the angle between them is $\frac\pi3$. (Angles are in radians.)

Find the exact length of the arc at the top of the door.

A two-metre-wide arched door in a restaurant is in the shape of a rectangle with a segment of a circle above it. The top of the door is the arc of a circle with radius 2 metres and its centre is in the middle of the base of the door. As shown in the diagram, the radii to the top corners of the door each make an angle of $\frac\pi3$ with the base, and the angle between them is $\frac\pi3$. (Angles are in radians.)

Calculate the exact area of the door.
questions.answer:
The door is the sector between the two radii plus the two right-angled triangles on either side (each with base 1, hypotenuse 2 and height $\sqrt3$):
$$\text{Sector} = \frac12(2^2)\frac\pi3 = \frac{2\pi}{3}, \qquad \text{each triangle} = \frac12(1)(2)\sin\frac\pi3 = \frac{\sqrt3}{2}.$$
$$\text{Area} = \frac{2\pi}{3} + \sqrt3\ \text{m}^2.$$

questions.question: It is known that $y = h(x)$ is an odd function of degree 5 which has a double root at $x = 2$ and which has a leading coefficient of 2. Draw a sketch of $y = h(x)$.
questions.answer:
Odd, so it passes through the origin and the double root at $x = 2$ is matched by one at $x = -2$:
$$h(x) = 2x(x - 2)^2(x + 2)^2.$$
It rises to the right, touches the $x$-axis at $\pm2$, crosses at the origin with positive gradient, and has point symmetry about the origin.

The table shows the future value of an annuity of \$1 for a variety of periods and interest rates. The contributions are made at the end of each year.

| Years | 5% | 6% | 7% | 8% | 9% | 10% | 11% | 12% |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 6 | 6.802 | 6.975 | 7.153 | 7.336 | 7.523 | 7.716 | 7.913 | 8.115 |
| 7 | 8.142 | 8.394 | 8.654 | 8.923 | 9.200 | 9.487 | 9.783 | 10.089 |
| 8 | 9.549 | 9.897 | 10.260 | 10.637 | 11.028 | 11.436 | 11.859 | 12.300 |
| 9 | 11.027 | 11.491 | 11.978 | 12.488 | 13.021 | 13.579 | 14.164 | 14.776 |
| 10 | 12.578 | 13.181 | 13.816 | 14.487 | 15.193 | 15.937 | 16.722 | 17.549 |
| 11 | 14.207 | 14.972 | 15.784 | 16.645 | 17.560 | 18.531 | 19.561 | 20.655 |
| 12 | 15.917 | 16.870 | 17.888 | 18.977 | 20.141 | 21.384 | 22.713 | 24.133 |

Penny invested a sum of \$3500 at the end of each year into an annuity that paid 9% pa and continued to do so for 12 years.

After 5 years had passed, she decided that she needed to invest in a second annuity so that the total value of the two investments when the first annuity matured would be \$100 000. The best interest rate that she could obtain for the second annuity was 6% pa.

What was the total yearly amount that Penny paid into the two annuities from the sixth year until the twelfth year?
questions.answer:
First annuity (12 years at 9%): $3500 \times 20.141 = \$70\,493.50$.

Needed from the second annuity: $100\,000 - 70\,493.50 = \$29\,506.50$, over 7 years (years 6–12) at 6% (factor 8.394):
$$C = \frac{29\,506.50}{8.394} \approx \$3515.19.$$
Total yearly amount for years 6–12: $3500 + 3515.19 = \$7015.19$.

The diagram shows half a closed cylinder with radius $r$ and height $h$ (the solid is cut along a diameter, so it has two semicircular ends, a curved face and a flat rectangular face). The total surface area of the shape is $\sqrt[3]{27\pi}$.

Show that the volume, $V$, can be expressed as
$$V = \frac{\pi}{2(\pi + 2)}\left[\sqrt[3]{27\pi}\,r - \pi r^3\right].$$
questions.answer:
Let $S = \sqrt[3]{27\pi}$. Surface area: two semicircles $\pi r^2$, curved face $\pi rh$, rectangle $2rh$:
$$S = \pi r^2 + \pi rh + 2rh \implies h = \frac{S - \pi r^2}{r(\pi + 2)}.$$
$$V = \frac12\pi r^2h = \frac{\pi r^2}{2} \cdot \frac{S - \pi r^2}{r(\pi + 2)} = \frac{\pi}{2(\pi + 2)}\left[Sr - \pi r^3\right].$$

questions.question:
The diagram shows half a closed cylinder with radius $r$ and height $h$ (the solid is cut along a diameter, so it has two semicircular ends, a curved face and a flat rectangular face). The total surface area of the shape is $\sqrt[3]{27\pi}$.

The volume is $V = \dfrac{\pi}{2(\pi + 2)}\left[\sqrt[3]{27\pi}\,r - \pi r^3\right]$. Hence, find the maximum volume.
questions.answer:
With $S = \sqrt[3]{27\pi} = 3\sqrt[3]\pi$:
$$\frac{dV}{dr} = \frac{\pi}{2(\pi + 2)}\left[S - 3\pi r^2\right] = 0 \implies r^2 = \frac{S}{3\pi} = \pi^{-\frac23} \implies r = \frac{1}{\sqrt[3]\pi}.$$
$\dfrac{d^2V}{dr^2} = \dfrac{\pi}{2(\pi + 2)}(-6\pi r) < 0$, so this is a maximum. Using $\pi r^2 = \frac S3$:
$$V_{\max} = \frac{\pi}{2(\pi + 2)} \cdot r\left(S - \frac S3\right) = \frac{\pi}{2(\pi + 2)} \cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt[3]\pi} \cdot 2\sqrt[3]\pi = \frac{\pi}{\pi + 2} \approx 0.611 \text{ units}^3.$$

The diagram shows the shaded area enclosed between the curves $y = 2\sin x$ and $y = 2\cos x$, between their intersections at $x = \frac\pi4$ and $x = \frac{5\pi}{4}$. Calculate the exact value of the shaded area.
questions.answer:
$2\sin x \ge 2\cos x$ on $\left[\frac\pi4, \frac{5\pi}{4}\right]$:
$$A = \int_{\pi/4}^{5\pi/4}(2\sin x - 2\cos x)\,dx = \Big[-2\cos x - 2\sin x\Big]_{\pi/4}^{5\pi/4} = \left(\sqrt2 + \sqrt2\right) - \left(-\sqrt2 - \sqrt2\right) = 4\sqrt2 \text{ square units}.$$

Mitch opened an investment account with an initial deposit of \$20 000 on 1st January 2023. The account earned interest at a rate of 8% per annum, compounding quarterly. He withdrew \$1000 on the 1st April 2023 and then on 1st July 2023 and continued to do so on the first day of each successive quarter. His withdrawals occurred after the quarterly interest was added. Let \$$A_n$ be the amount remaining in the account after $n$ withdrawals have been made.

$A_n = 50000 - 30000 \times 1.02^n$. What is the total number of withdrawals that Mitch could make before the account runs out of funds?
questions.answer:
$A_n = 0 \implies 1.02^n = \dfrac53 \implies n = \dfrac{\ln(5/3)}{\ln 1.02} \approx 25.8$.

Mitch can make **25** full withdrawals of \$1000 (a 26th, partial withdrawal would then empty the account).
